report.source_text: The patient underwent additional pelvic and transvaginal ultrasound, an abdominal and pelvic CT, and a pelvic MRI with and without intravenous contrast. The MRI findings revealed a solid mass measuring 10.5 × 9.5 × 11.3 cm anterior to the uterine fundus with numerous internal non-enhancing cystic spaces. The mass slightly abuts the anterior uterine fundus but appears to cause mass effect on the uterus. Immediately inferior to this 11 cm mass, a tubular cystic lesion measuring 3.2 × 5.2 × 5.3 cm was found. The uterus was also found to be anteverted, slightly anteflexed, and normal-sized. The findings also included a right ovarian cyst measuring 1.1 cm. The 11 cm solid mass was presumed to represent a pedunculated partially necrotic fibroid that had torsed and disconnected from the uterus. Radiology recommended surgical resection.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old postmenopausal woman presented to the emergency department with acute onset intense pelvic and abdominal pain radiating to the lower back, vomiting, and diarrhea. Initial transabdominal ultrasound revealed large uterine fibroids (10.1 × 9.7 × 11.5 cm) and was negative for kidney stones; CBC, CMP, and urinalysis were normal. She was admitted for observation, improved overnight, and was discharged with planned office follow-up. A few days later, she returned to her OB-GYN with recurrent severe pain in the lower abdomen, right groin, and right buttock with occasional nausea. Follow-up imaging (pelvic ultrasound, CT, and pelvic MRI with contrast) revealed an 11 cm solid mass anterior to the uterine fundus with numerous internal non-enhancing cystic spaces, initially presumed to represent a pedunculated partially necrotic fibroid that had torsed and disconnected from the uterus. Radiology recommended surgical resection. Intraoperatively, a partially torsioned right adnexal mass measuring 14 × 10 × 10 cm with extensive cystic degeneration and hemorrhage was identified, with the right ovary not observed separate from the mass. The intraoperative diagnosis was right ovarian fibroma (not uterine leiomyoma as preoperative imaging had suggested). Specimens were sent to pathology and cytology; cytology and pathology reports were negative for malignancy. The postoperative hospital course was uneventful, and follow-up was scheduled for one week after surgery.
